problems.source_says: 30 and 30. The form records 60 analyzed at the study level, from t(58) and no reported exclusions. With 30 randomized per arm, 60 analyzed leaves no split but 30/30. The printed statistics also fix the split: only 30/30 reproduces t(58) = -1.897 from the printed means and SDs (29/31 gives -1.877, 31/29 gives -1.914), the similarity Welch df of 48.36, and all five Mann-Whitney r values (n1 x n2 = 900). If form-spec rule 1 is read to require null here, the study-level 60 rests on the same evidence and should be null too, so the two levels disagree either way. Reconciled sibling forms fill arm n_analyzed on the same kind of evidence: c127 (60 people, 20/20/20, exclusions 'None reported', outcome N not printed) and c096, second study (51/50/51 from the allocation sentences and the ANOVA df).
problems.quote: These individuals were randomly assigned into two conditions, with 30 participants per condition.

confirmed.statement: One between-subjects study. 60 people were recruited on Prolific and randomly assigned, 30 per condition. participants.n_randomized = 60 and arms[].n_randomized = 30 and 30 are right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 ('A between-subjects design was used'), Section 3.2, Section 3.3

confirmed.statement: Figure 1, the experiment workflow, prints N = 60 above the pre-survey and N = 30 above each condition (orange C_after: 10 min alone, then 10 min with the LLM; green C_before: 20 min with the LLM). It prints no N at the post-survey and shows no dropouts. Assignment came after the pre-survey and the practice task ('Afterward, the participants were randomly assigned'), so all 60 were randomized.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Figure 1 and caption; PDF p. 3, Section 3.3

confirmed.statement: participants.n_analyzed = 60 is supported. The abstract and the introduction report results from 'a controlled experiment with 60 participants', and the idea-quantity test has 58 df. With 30 per arm, the printed means and SDs give t(58) = -1.897, d = -0.490, p = 0.063, exactly as printed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF p. 7, Section 4.1

confirmed.statement: The other two coded outcomes also fit 30 per arm. For similarity, the printed SDs give Welch df = 48.37 at 30/30 (printed 48.36), against 46.13 at 29/31. For diversity, the printed t/d ratio (1.337/0.345) matches sqrt(30/2): t = 1.336 at 30 per arm and 1.314 at 29.

All five Mann-Whitney tests fit r = 2U/900 - 1: U = 289.5, 267.5, 227.0, 304.0 and 628.5 give -0.357, -0.406, -0.496, -0.324 and 0.397, as printed. So n1 x n2 = 900, which with 60 people means 30 x 30. A 29 x 31 split misses four of the five.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Sections 4.2.1 and 4.2.3; PDF p. 8, Section 4.2.4

confirmed.statement: The counts are people, not ideas or ratings. The demographics cover 60 people (26 female, 34 male). Each coded outcome is one score per participant (Table 1 output: 'Similarity score for each P_i'), and the test df are participant-level. counts_are = people and n_units = null fit.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2; PDF p. 5, Sections 3.5.2 to 3.5.4; PDF p. 6, Table 1; PDF p. 7, Section 4.1

confirmed.statement: No exclusions, attention-check failures, dropouts, or replacements are reported anywhere. Completion time was recorded 'To check whether participants engaged in the ideation task', but no one is reported excluded on it. The on-screen warning that the back button 'will lead to task failure' is the only sign that a start could fail, and the paper reports no failures. exclusions = 'None reported' is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1 to 16; PDF p. 4, Figure 2; PDF p. 5, Section 3.5.1

confirmed.statement: The within-arm Wilcoxon pre-post tests imply 24 nonzero pairs in C_before and 28 in C_after, and z reproduces exactly at those n (2.271 and 0.273). This fits 30 per arm with zero differences dropped. The form codes no outcome from these tests.

confirmed.statement: No person is counted twice. The paper has one study, each person did one condition on one counterbalanced topic, and the practice task that all 60 did is not analyzed.

No other paper is reported to use these participants. The PDF mentions no earlier or companion use. In the candidate set, c023 (a review) and c094 (which adapts a scale) only cite this paper. arXiv 2502.06197 has one version (v1, 10 Feb 2025, 1,716 KB, journal-ref CHI '25 Article 25, pp. 1-16), and the merged Semantic Scholar record for doi 10.1145/3706598.3713146 has the same abstract count of 60. The ACM full text returned HTTP 403, so the version of record was not compared page by page.

summary: The PDF supports every people count the form records: one between-subjects study randomized 60 Prolific participants, 30 per condition, reports no exclusions, analyzed all 60 (the printed t(58), Welch df, and Mann-Whitney r values fit only 30 per arm), counts people rather than ideas, and shares its sample with no other study or paper. The one defect is that arms[].n_analyzed is null although the form records 60 analyzed at the study level on the same evidence, which fixes each arm at 30, and this detail leaves criterion 2 met with 60 people analyzed.
